close_reason: Done in commit. Replaced format!("{:?}", kind) with format!("{kind:?}").
description: pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:167 — `s.serialize_str(&format!("{:?}", kind))` uses the positional format-string form. Rust 1.58+ supports captured identifiers; clippy::uninlined_format_args (pedantic, on by default in many house lint configs) flags this and prefers `format!("{kind:?}")`. Inconsistency check: the rest of the diff uses the inlined form throughout (e.g., `panic!("expected MalformedAnchor(0), got {other:?}")` at fixtures.rs:191, `write!(f, "i/o error: {e}")` at lib.rs:242), so this one line is the outlier. Fix: `s.serialize_str(&format!("{kind:?}"))` or, while there, drop the intermediate String entirely with `s.collect_str(&format_args!("{kind:?}"))` to avoid the heap allocation. What goes wrong if it stays: micro-readability inconsistency with the rest of the crate; clippy::pedantic warning.
title: format!("{:?}", kind) uses positional format args instead of inlined form
